facts.text: Keystone was founded in 1906 when the Union Pacific Railroad built a branch line through the North Platte Valley, turning a ranching outpost into a town by 1910.
The town’s name comes from William Paxton Sr.’s ranch brand, as the land he deeded to the public in 1906 became the site of Keystone.
Keystone’s Little Church, built 1907‑08, features dual Catholic and Protestant altars and reversible pews, a design that earned it a National Register of Historic Places listing in 1979.
Keystone sits at about 3,100 feet above sea level, placing it among the higher elevations of Nebraska’s North Platte River valley.
Community life in early Keystone revolved around a church, a 1910 hotel with a dance hall, and a library founded in 1908, reflecting settlers’ resilience amid isolation.
